question: What is software engineering?
ground_truth_answer: Software engineering is the disciplined and organized approach to the development, operation, maintenance and evolution of software.
ground_truth_context:
What is Software Engineering?
• Software engineering is the disciplined and organized approach to the
development, operation, maintenance, and evolution of software.
• A software product is not only the program code. It also includes:
• Requirements
• Design documents
• Test cases
• User manuals
• Maintenance support
• Updates and improvements

question: What is a program?
ground_truth_answer: A program is a set of instructions written in a programming language to perform a task.
ground_truth_context:
Software
vs
Program
Program
• A program is a set of instructions written in a
programming language to perform a task.
• Example:
• a C program that calculates student grades, a
Java program that prints a report, a Python script
that sorts data
Software
• Software is broader than a program. It includes:
• the executable program, configuration files,
documentation, test data, installation support,
interfaces, update mechanisms, maintenance
processes

question: How does software differ from a program?
ground_truth_answer: Software is broader than a program: a complete deliverable that includes code, documentation, testing, maintenance and user support, and it is expected to evolve over time.
ground_truth_context:
| Program | Software |
| --- | --- |
| Usually a coding artifact | A complete deliverable product |
| Focuses mainly on instructions | Includes code, docs, testing, maintenance, and user support |
| May be created by one person for a small task | Usually built for users, organizations, or large-scale needs |
| Can be short-term | Often expected to evolve over time |

question: Why is software engineering important for managing complexity?
ground_truth_answer: Small programs can be written informally but large systems cannot. With many modules, users, developers and requirements a systematic approach is essential.
ground_truth_context:
Reasons why software engineering matters
To manage complexity
• Small programs can sometimes be written informally. Large
systems cannot.
When many modules, users, developers, and requirements are
involved, a systematic approach is essential.
To improve quality
• Users expect software to be: Correct, dependable, secure, efficient,
easy to use, Without engineering practices, quality becomes
inconsistent.

question: What does the term software crisis refer to?
ground_truth_answer: The long-standing problems that occurred when software systems became larger and more complex but development methods were weak, unstructured and poorly managed.
ground_truth_context:
The Software Crisis
The term software crisis refers to the long-standing problems that occurred when software
systems became larger and more complex, but development methods were weak,
unstructured, and poorly managed.
Main problems of the software crisis
• projects delivered late
• projects exceeded budgets
• software failed to meet user needs
• software was hard to maintain
• software contained many errors
• documentation was poor
• changes were difficult and expensive

question: Why do software projects still fail today?
ground_truth_answer: Unclear requirements, poor communication, unrealistic deadlines, weak design, insufficient testing and lack of user involvement.
ground_truth_context:
Why did the crisis happen?
• As computer systems grew in size and importance, many developers still relied on informal
programming practices. This created serious problems in quality and project control.
• Is the software crisis over?
• Not completely.
Today, tools, methods, testing, agile practices, and standards are much better than before. However,
many projects still fail because of:
• Unclear requirements
• Poor communication
• Unrealistic deadlines
• Weak design
• Insufficient testing
• Lack of user involvement

question: What activities does a software engineer contribute to besides coding?
ground_truth_answer: Requirements understanding, analysis and problem solving, design, implementation, testing, documentation, and maintenance and evolution.
ground_truth_context:
Role of a Software Engineer
• A software engineer is not just a coder. In practice, software engineers contribute to multiple activities.
Requirements understanding: Work with users, clients, and stakeholders to understand what the system
should do.
Analysis and problem solving: Study the problem carefully and identify suitable software-based solutions.
Design: Plan the system structure, modules, interfaces, and overall solution.
Implementation: Write code and develop the actual software components.
Testing: Check whether the software works correctly and meets requirements.
Documentation: Prepare technical documents, user guides, and other supporting materials.
Maintenance and evolution: Fix errors, improve features, and update the system according to new needs.
Team collaboration: Work and communicate effectively with developers, testers, project managers, clients, and
other stakeholders.

question: What professional expectations should a software engineer demonstrate?
ground_truth_answer: Technical competence, responsibility, honesty, respect for privacy and security, and awareness of ethical and legal issues.
ground_truth_context:
Professional
expectations

Responsibility
Honesty

question: Give examples of software engineering ethics.
ground_truth_answer: Not stealing code illegally, not misusing private data, not hiding major defects knowingly, not making false claims about system quality, and not ignoring safety issues in critical systems.
ground_truth_context:
What are software engineering ethics?
• These are the moral and professional responsibilities software engineers
should follow when developing and deploying software.
Examples
• A software engineer should:
• Not steal code illegally
• Not misuse private data
• Not hide major defects knowingly
• Not make false claims about system quality
• Not ignore safety issues in critical systems

question: What should students include in the in-class software proposal?
ground_truth_answer: A problem statement, proposed solution, key features, possible risks, quality expectations and a basic development approach.
ground_truth_context:
In Class Activity
• Give students a system idea and ask them to prepare a small software
proposal as if they are presenting to management or a client.
• Students should include:
• Problem statement
• Proposed solution
• Key features
• Possible risks
• Quality expectations
• Basic development approach
